data.text/markdown:
1. The Question

The operations manager would use this tool to understand what happened in the business over the past week. It gives a quick view of sales, popular products, and any orders that still need attention. The tool helps the manager decide whether sales are performing well, which products are driving demand, and whether there are unshipped orders that need follow-up.

2. My Plan Before AI

steps:
  1. Calculate the date range for the last 7 days.
  2. Connect to the API and request all orders in that date range.
  3. Check pagination and keep requesting pages until all orders are collected.
  4. Loop through the orders to calculate total orders, total revenue, revenue by country, and unshipped orders.
  5. Connect to the API again for each order to get its line items.
  6. Loop through the line items to count units sold by product.
  7. Find the top 5 products.
  8. Build the report and write the manager summary sentence.
questions:
  1. Which functions will your tool need? For each, what goes in and what comes out?
suggested from the problem:
  • date.today() Input: none Output: today's date
  • timedelta(days=6) Input: number of days Output: a time difference used to calculate the start date
  • str(date) Input: a date object Output: a date string in the format YYYY-MM-DD
  • get_orders(from_date, to_date) Input: start date, end date Output: list of orders
Additional:
  • get_order_details(order_id) Input: order ID Output: order line items
  • summarize_orders(orders) Input: list of orders Output: order count total revenue revenue by country unshipped orders
  • count_product_sales(order_details) Input: order line items Output: units sold by product
  • get_top_products(product_sales) Input: product sales totals Output: top 5 products
  1. Which addresses will they request?
  • /shop/orders to get all orders in the date range
  • /shop/orders/{order_id} to get the line items for each order
  1. How will you know you have every record?
  • Check the pagination information returned by the API.
  • Compare the number of orders collected with the total number of orders reported in pagination.
  • Continue requesting pages until those numbers match.
  1. Which check will you use in section 6, and which two numbers should agree?
  • A sum total amount from an order's line items should agree with the order’s total from /shop/orders.

data.text/markdown:
6. How I Know These Numbers Are Right

I checked four things a second way, all shown in the cells below: 1. Did I collect every order? In step 3, the API's pagination said there were 35 orders total in this date range. I collected orders page by page and counted 35 orders in my orders list. 35 equals 35, so I have every order, not just the first page. 2. Does each order's line-item total agree with its reported order total? An order's order_total_dollars (from /shop/orders) should equal the sum of its line_total_dollars values (from /shop/orders/{order_id}), since the order total is just all its lines added up. I checked this for all 35 orders: I summed each order's lines separately and compared that sum to the order's reported total, allowing a one-cent gap for rounding. 0 of 35 orders disagreed, so the revenue and line-item numbers in this report agree with each other. 3. Did I collect every line item? Each order in /shop/orders already reports its own line_count, a count of how many line items it has. I summed line_count across all 35 orders and compared it to the number of line items I actually collected in step 5. Both came to 1065, so step 6 and step 7, which depend on having every line item, are built on a complete set. 4. Does the units-sold total in product_sales agree with the raw line items? I summed the units two different ways: once by adding up every value already stored in the product_sales dictionary (built in step 6), and once by going back to order_lines directly and adding up every quantity field. Both came to 25,671 units, so building the dictionary did not drop or double-count anything. 5. Are the top 5 products really the top 5? The picking method in step 7 works by repeatedly scanning for the highest remaining count, so it should be correct by construction, but I checked it a different way anyway: I took the 5th-place product's count (446 units) and scanned every other product not in the top 5 to see if any of them actually sold more. None did, which confirms the top 5 list is right.

7. Working With the Agent

I did one sanity check in step 3 as explained in section 6, then when we were at step 5, ai suggested doing the planned check right there instead of waiting until step 7 as originally planned. I agreed thus we knew at that point everything was fine. That was check #2. But doing that also made me realized doing that as a check point left step 6 - 7 unaudited so I told ai to find a way to check those steps. It suggested check #3, which still did not help audit anything beyond step 5. So I had to tell it to try again and focus on step 6 - 7 which was how I got check #4 - 5. I kept check #3 anyway as it doesn't really hurt anything.
